phase: 15.4 — bounded parallel ingest: worker-count sweep + determinism witness
measured_commit_subject: phase15.3: packed-store receipt — 111x fewer files, 0.72x bytes, parity latency, identity unchanged
measured_binary: target/release/vole-document (built --all-features, so the non-default `parallel` feature is on)
corpus: real100-v1 SUBSET: 10 documents including a 54 MB PDF and package formats (NOT the frozen 100-document population)
what_is_measured: one `encode` per document, then `field-ingest --workers N` for N in {1,2,4,8,16}; wall time per N, plus a determinism witness (identical field id and byte-exact `materialize --exact` across every N)

speedup_vs_serial.reading: no measurable speedup: the parallelised stages (Flate length-probing, ObjStm precompute, package-member encode) are not the ingest bottleneck on this subset; the median document is dominated by serial store I/O and small-document fixed cost

determinism_witness.reading: a genuine POSITIVE: the parallel path is exactly as deterministic as serial, which is the precondition for ever adopting it

outlier.hypothesis: peak-RSS growth under the ObjStm precompute (the design's own stated risk: extra threads raise peak RSS against a 6g cap with zram swap), or scheduling noise; needs a dedicated investigation before parallelism could be adopted

interpretation: Parallelism as implemented is neutral-to-negative on speed and exactly safe on identity. Adopting it would require finding the true bottleneck first (profiling), not more parallelism.
lane_caveat: the lane is capped at cpus: 8, so --workers 8 saturates it and --workers 16 oversubscribes it; above-8 counts are informational
tuning: none; the subset is pre-registered, the worker counts are pre-registered
